heroHeadline: Colombia: Cepeda Wins First Round, Runoff vs. De la Espriella June 21; US-Iran Deal Still Unsigned Day 3, IRGC Issues Blockade Attack Warning; Hormuz Closed Week 14
heroSubtitle: May 31, 2026 — Iván Cepeda won the first round of Colombia's presidential election with approximately 44-45% of the vote, heading to a June 21 runoff against conservative Abelardo De la Espriella (~31%). The ELN's 4-day election ceasefire held throughout voting day with no significant violence. The June 21 runoff will determine whether Colombia's peace architecture — ELN talks, JEP, FARC-EMC process — survives: Cepeda pledges to resume all negotiations; De la Espriella pledges to immediately end them. President Petro's term ends today. On the US-Iran front, the deal tentatively confirmed by CNN on May 28 remains unsigned three days later: CNBC reported Trump ended a May 29 White House meeting on Iran without announcing any 'final determination,' and IRGC General Rezaei escalated on May 30 by warning that Iran would 'attack the blockade' if Trump betrays the framework. The Strait of Hormuz enters its 14th week of closure with ~750 vessels trapped and ~$6B/month in Iranian oil exports blocked. The Lebanon-Israel political track (Round 4) meets June 2-3 in Washington — next critical milestone as the 45-day ceasefire extension counts toward ~June 29 expiry. Ukraine-Russia June 2 Istanbul Round 2 is tomorrow; a 1,200-for-1,200 prisoner exchange is reportedly in the works but Russia rejected an unconditional ceasefire.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
